--- title: "Cam Ward's passing yards rose in every season in the data and beat the opponent-adjusted baseline each time" date: "2026-11-05" description: "Cam Ward's passing yardage climbed each season from 2021 to 2024, and it stayed above the league baseline for opponents of the same strength in all four." followups: - "Position-specific baselines: compare each passer only with other quarterbacks, not every player with a passing line." - "Carry the opponent band into the season arcs, so a rise in yardage can be read against the schedule it was earned on." - "Extend the arcs to the 2010 to 2013 seasons once game-level stats cover them, so early careers are not cut off at the start of the data." author: - "AI directed by Nick Giangreco" freeze: auto vignette: > %\VignetteIndexEntry{Cam Ward's passing yards rose in every season in the data and beat the opponent-adjusted baseline each time} %\VignetteEngine{quarto::html} %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8} --- ::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"} *Data as of the `data-latest` release, retrieved 2026-11-05. Careers of recent classes are right-censored; later seasons may not yet be present.* ::: ## 1. Introduction A quarterback's yardage moves from season to season and game to game, and opponent strength is one reason. This post follows the passing yards of five recent college quarterbacks and asks whether each season beat the league baseline for opponents of the same strength. + *Expectation one: Cam Ward's passing yards rose in every season in the data.* + *Expectation two: passing yardage falls modestly as opponent Elo rises.* + *Expectation three: Cam Ward's yardage beat the opponent-adjusted baseline each season, while Jordan Travis's fell below it in two.* ## 2. Data ### 2.1 Each game is set against the league baseline for its opponent strength Each player-game is compared with the average for the same season and opponent band. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} tibble::tribble( ~Term , ~Meaning , "Season arc" , "Season total of passing yards, one per season.", "Season index" , "The player's n-th season with a stat line in the data.", "Opponent band" , "The opponent's pregame Elo: under 1400, 1400 to 1599, 1600 to 1799, 1800 and up, or unrated (no Elo).", "Baseline" , "Mean yards for that season, band, and stat across all passers.", "Residual" , "A game's yards minus its baseline." ) |> kable(caption = "The terms used in the post.") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} Table: The terms used in the post. |Term |Meaning | |:-------------|:-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------| |Season arc |Season total of passing yards, one per season. | |Season index |The player's n-th season with a stat line in the data. | |Opponent band |The opponent's pregame Elo: under 1400, 1400 to 1599, 1600 to 1799, 1800 and up, or unrated (no Elo). | |Baseline |Mean yards for that season, band, and stat across all passers. | |Residual |A game's yards minus its baseline. | ::: ::: ## 3. Results ### 3.1 Cam Ward's passing yards rose in every season in the data *Expectation: his yardage rose in each season, and no other cast member's did.* ✅ Only Ward's arc climbs at every step among the five cast members. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} cast_qb |> arrange(.data$who, .data$season) |> transmute( Player = .data$who, Season = .data$season, `Season index` = .data$season_index, Team = .data$team, `Passing yards` = fmt(.data$value) ) |> kable(caption = "Season passing yards for the five cast quarterbacks.") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} Table: Season passing yards for the five cast quarterbacks. |Player | Season| Season index|Team |Passing yards | |:--------------|------:|------------:|:----------------|:-------------| |Cam Ward | 2021| 1|Incarnate Word |376 | |Cam Ward | 2022| 2|Washington State |3,218 | |Cam Ward | 2023| 3|Washington State |3,732 | |Cam Ward | 2024| 4|Miami |4,313 | |Joe Burrow | 2016| 1|Ohio State |226 | |Joe Burrow | 2017| 2|Ohio State |61 | |Joe Burrow | 2018| 3|LSU |2,893 | |Joe Burrow | 2019| 4|LSU |5,671 | |Jordan Travis | 2018| 1|Louisville |71 | |Jordan Travis | 2019| 2|Florida State |79 | |Jordan Travis | 2020| 3|Florida State |1,056 | |Jordan Travis | 2021| 4|Florida State |1,539 | |Jordan Travis | 2022| 5|Florida State |3,214 | |Jordan Travis | 2023| 6|Florida State |2,745 | |Kyle Allen | 2014| 1|Texas A&M |1,322 | |Kyle Allen | 2015| 2|Texas A&M |2,210 | |Kyle Allen | 2017| 3|Houston |751 | |Shane Buechele | 2016| 1|Texas |2,958 | |Shane Buechele | 2017| 2|Texas |1,405 | |Shane Buechele | 2018| 3|Texas |273 | |Shane Buechele | 2019| 4|SMU |3,930 | |Shane Buechele | 2020| 5|SMU |3,095 | ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} p <- cast_qb |> ggplot(aes(.data$season_index, .data$value, colour = .data$who)) + geom_line(linewidth = 1.2) + geom_point_interactive( aes(tooltip = paste0(.data$who, ", ", .data$season, ": ", fmt(.data$value), " yards")) ) + labs(x = "Season index", y = "Passing yards", colour = NULL) + theme_minimal(base_size = 14) girafe(ggobj = p, width_svg = 13, height_svg = 6) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} p <- cast_qb |> mutate(label = paste0(.data$who, " (", .data$season, ")")) |> ggplot(aes(.data$season, .data$value, colour = .data$who)) + geom_point_interactive( aes(tooltip = paste0(.data$who, ", ", .data$season, ": ", fmt(.data$value), " yards")), size = 4 ) + labs(x = "Season", y = "Passing yards", colour = NULL) + theme_minimal(base_size = 14) girafe(ggobj = p, width_svg = 13, height_svg = 6) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ### 3.2 Passing yardage falls modestly as opponent Elo rises *Expectation: raw yardage decreases from the weakest to the strongest rated band.* ✅ Raw yards drop by about 16 a game from the weakest rated band to the strongest, and unrated opponents sit near the bottom. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} band_yds |> transmute( `Opponent band` = .data$opponent_elo_band, `Passer games` = fmt(.data$games), `Mean passing yards` = fmt(.data$mean_yds, 1) ) |> kable(caption = "Mean passing yards per game by opponent band, all passers.") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} Table: Mean passing yards per game by opponent band, all passers. |Opponent band |Passer games |Mean passing yards | |:-------------|:------------|:------------------| |Under 1400 |8,319 |212.2 | |1400 to 1599 |7,996 |209.4 | |1600 to 1799 |6,231 |205.3 | |1800 and up |3,127 |195.9 | |Unrated |9,608 |193.8 | ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} p <- band_yds |> mutate( opponent_elo_band = factor(.data$opponent_elo_band, band_levels), tooltip = paste0(.data$opponent_elo_band, ": ", fmt(.data$mean_yds, 1), " yards") ) |> ggplot(aes(.data$opponent_elo_band, .data$mean_yds, fill = .data$opponent_elo_band == "Unrated")) + geom_col_interactive(aes(tooltip = .data$tooltip), show.legend = FALSE) + scale_fill_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "#4C78A8", `TRUE` = "#9CA3AF")) + labs(x = "Opponent band", y = "Mean passing yards per game") + theme_minimal(base_size = 14) girafe(ggobj = p, width_svg = 13, height_svg = 6) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} p <- pass_games |> group_by(.data$season, .data$opponent_elo_band) |> summarise(mean_yds = mean(.data$value), games = dplyr::n(), .groups = "drop") |> ggplot(aes(.data$season, .data$mean_yds, colour = .data$opponent_elo_band)) + geom_point_interactive( aes(tooltip = paste0(.data$season, ", ", .data$opponent_elo_band, ": ", fmt(.data$mean_yds, 1), " yards over ", fmt(.data$games), " games")), size = 3 ) + labs(x = "Season", y = "Mean passing yards per game", colour = "Opponent band") + theme_minimal(base_size = 14) girafe(ggobj = p, width_svg = 13, height_svg = 6) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ### 3.3 Cam Ward beat the opponent-adjusted baseline each season, and Jordan Travis fell below it twice *Expectation: Ward's residuals are positive in every season, and Travis's are negative in two.* ✅ The residual averages a player's gains over the baseline season by season. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} cast_res |> arrange(.data$who, .data$season) |> transmute( Player = .data$who, Season = .data$season, Games = .data$games, `Mean residual (yards)` = fmt(.data$mean_resid, 1) ) |> kable(caption = "Mean passing-yard residual per game, by cast player and season.") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} Table: Mean passing-yard residual per game, by cast player and season. |Player | Season| Games|Mean residual (yards) | |:--------------|------:|-----:|:---------------------| |Cam Ward | 2021| 1|191.0 | |Cam Ward | 2022| 13|33.9 | |Cam Ward | 2023| 12|103.3 | |Cam Ward | 2024| 13|127.3 | |Joe Burrow | 2018| 12|33.7 | |Joe Burrow | 2019| 15|185.5 | |Jordan Travis | 2020| 6|-40.9 | |Jordan Travis | 2021| 7|-27.5 | |Jordan Travis | 2022| 13|34.3 | |Jordan Travis | 2023| 10|61.0 | |Kyle Allen | 2014| 5|-1.9 | |Kyle Allen | 2015| 9|26.7 | |Kyle Allen | 2017| 3|30.6 | |Shane Buechele | 2016| 11|52.6 | |Shane Buechele | 2017| 5|46.9 | |Shane Buechele | 2018| 1|-2.2 | |Shane Buechele | 2019| 12|85.7 | |Shane Buechele | 2020| 10|93.8 | ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} p <- cast_res |> mutate( tooltip = paste0(.data$who, ", ", .data$season, ": ", fmt(.data$mean_resid, 1), " yards over baseline") ) |> ggplot(aes(.data$season, .data$mean_resid, fill = .data$who)) + geom_col_interactive(aes(tooltip = .data$tooltip), position = "dodge") + geom_hline(yintercept = 0) + labs(x = "Season", y = "Mean residual (yards per game)", fill = NULL) + theme_minimal(base_size = 14) girafe(ggobj = p, width_svg = 13, height_svg = 6) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} p <- gp |> filter(.data$stat == "pass_yds") |> inner_join(subjects, by = c(playerId = "cfb_athlete_id")) |> ggplot(aes(.data$season, .data$residual, colour = .data$who)) + geom_point_interactive( aes(tooltip = paste0(.data$who, ", ", .data$season, ", week ", .data$week, " vs ", .data$opponent, ": ", fmt(.data$residual), " yards")), size = 2.5 ) + geom_hline(yintercept = 0) + labs(x = "Season", y = "Residual (yards in the game)", colour = NULL) + theme_minimal(base_size = 14) girafe(ggobj = p, width_svg = 13, height_svg = 6) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ## 4. Summary Cam Ward's arc is the only one among the five that rose at every step, and his yardage stayed above baseline in each season. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} tibble::tribble( ~Expectation , ~Verdict , ~Evidence , "Ward's passing yards rose in every season" , "✅" , "376, 3,218, 3,732, 4,313 yards (2021 to 2024)" , "Passing yardage falls modestly as opponent Elo rises" , "✅" , "About 16 yards per game, weakest to strongest rated band" , "Ward above baseline each season; Travis below in two" , "✅" , "Ward positive in all four seasons; Travis negative in 2020 and 2021" ) |> kable(caption = "Each expectation and what the data showed.") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} Table: Each expectation and what the data showed. |Expectation |Verdict |Evidence | |:----------------------------------------------------|:-------|:-------------------------------------------------------------------| |Ward's passing yards rose in every season |✅ |376, 3,218, 3,732, 4,313 yards (2021 to 2024) | |Passing yardage falls modestly as opponent Elo rises |✅ |About 16 yards per game, weakest to strongest rated band | |Ward above baseline each season; Travis below in two |✅ |Ward positive in all four seasons; Travis negative in 2020 and 2021 | ::: ::: ## 5. Discussion ::: {.callout-important} Ward's residuals stayed positive, so his yardage beat the baseline for opponents of the same strength in every season. The baseline compares every passer, so it cannot separate a quarterback's own play from the offense around him. ::: Caveats: unrated opponents (no Elo, mostly lower-division teams) are kept as their own band rather than dropped; about 27% of player-games fall there. The data begin in 2010, so a career's first season in the data is not necessarily its first season in college. Five players is a snapshot, not a sample.
